Multisite Analysis of Neurologic Disease and HMPV

  • Show All Code

Expanding the Single-Site Pittsburgh Findings (2024)

Author
Affiliation

Ray Pomponio, for Dr. Anna Wang-Erickson

Children’s Hospital of Pittsburgh

Published

October 9, 2026

Study Summary

We expanded the single-site Pittsburgh analysis (2024) to the full multisite NVSN cohort to investigate whether children with neurologic/neuromuscular disease experience disproportionately higher risk of human metapneumovirus (HMPV) infection and disease severity. Previous single-site findings showed neurologic disease was associated with 1.75× higher odds of HMPV infection (95% CI: 1.19, 2.56) and 4.80× higher odds of elevated severity (95% CI: 2.01, 11.47). This multisite analysis (136,156 cases across 7 sites, 2016–2026) adjusts for demographics, comorbidities, and geographic variation to assess whether neurologic conditions confer disproportionate risk in a larger, more generalizable cohort.

Introduction

This report presents a multisite analysis extending our 2024 single-site (Pittsburgh) findings on the association between neurologic/neuromuscular disease and human metapneumovirus (HMPV) infection and disease severity. We leverage 136,156 pediatric acute respiratory infection (ARI) cases across 7 NVSN sites over 10+ years (2016–2026) to investigate whether neurologic conditions represent a consistent, significant risk factor for HMPV infection and severe outcomes in a larger, more representative cohort.

Previous Findings (Pittsburgh, 2024)

In our single-site analysis, we found: - HMPV infection risk: Children with neurologic/neuromuscular disease had 1.75× higher odds of HMPV infection (95% CI: 1.19, 2.56) - HMPV disease severity: Among HMPV-positive cases, neurologic disease was associated with 4.80× higher odds of elevated severity (95% CI: 2.01, 11.47)

Research Questions

Primary: Is neurologic/neuromuscular disease associated with increased HMPV infection risk in a multisite cohort (adjusting for demographics, comorbidities, site)?

Secondary: Among HMPV-positive children, is neurologic disease associated with elevated disease severity (5-level ordinal outcome)?

Methods

Data & Study Population

Data are from the New Vaccine Surveillance Network (NVSN) multisite surveillance network covering pediatric ARI cases from 7 sites (Vanderbilt, Rochester, Cincinnati, Seattle, Houston, Kansas City, Pittsburgh) over study years 2–11 (2016–2026).

Inclusion criteria: All pediatric ARI cases with valid HMPV test results (tmpv ∈ {0, 1}).

Exclusion criteria: HMPV inconclusive or missing results (tmpv ∈ {8, 9, NA}).

Statistical Analysis

RQ1: HMPV Infection Risk

We assessed factors associated with HMPV infection status using generalized linear models (GLM) with binomial family and logit link. The primary exposure was neurologic/neuromuscular disease (c_unuerologic). Adjustment variables included age group, sex, race/ethnicity, insurance, chronic respiratory conditions, cardiovascular disease, immunosuppressive conditions, prematurity, study year, and study site.

Primary analysis used multiple imputation (m=5) for missing covariates, with estimates pooled per Rubin’s rules. Unadjusted (univariate) and adjusted (multivariable) odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) and Wald test p-values are reported.

RQ2: HMPV Severity Among Positive Cases

We assessed the association between neurologic disease and ordinal illness severity among HMPV-positive cases using proportional odds (ordinal logistic) regression. Outcome severity was defined as a 5-level ordinal composite: (1) ED/clinic discharge, (2) hospital admission without oxygen support, (3) hospital admission with oxygen support, (4) ICU admission without invasive mechanical ventilation/ECMO, (5) ICU with invasive mechanical ventilation/ECMO or death.

Adjustment variables included age group, sex, race/ethnicity, insurance, comorbidities (respiratory, cardiovascular, immunosuppressive, prematurity), co-infections, and study site. We tested the proportional odds assumption via Brant test and report violations as limitations.

# --- STEP 2: RECODE & DERIVE VARIABLES ---
setDT(dat.analyze)

# Age group (4 levels)
dat.analyze[, c_agegroup := fcase(
  c_ageyears < 1, 1,
  c_ageyears < 2, 2,
  c_ageyears < 3, 3,
  c_ageyears >= 3, 4
)]
dat.analyze[, c_agegroup := factor(
  c_agegroup, 4:1, c("3+ yrs", "2-3 yrs", "1-2 yrs", "<1 yr")
)]

# Sex
dat.analyze[, sexch := factor(sexch, 1:2, c("Male", "Female"))]

# Race/ethnicity (White NH as reference)
dat.analyze[, c_race_int := factor(
  c_race_int, c(1, 2, 3, 4), 
  c("WhiteNH", "BlackNH", "OtherNH", "Hispanic")
)]

# Insurance (Private as reference)
dat.analyze[, scrinsurance := factor(
  scrinsurance, c(2, 1, 3, 4),
  c("Private", "Public", "Both", "None")
)]

# Study year (ordered factor)
dat.analyze[, c_ariyear := factor(
  c_ariyear, 2:11, 
  c("Y2 (2016-17)", "Y3 (2017-18)", "Y4 (2018-19)", "Y5 (2019-20)",
    "Y6 (2020-21)", "Y7 (2021-22)", "Y8 (2022-23)", "Y9 (2023-24)",
    "Y10 (2024-25)", "Y11 (2025-26)")
)]

# Study site (Pittsburgh as reference)
dat.analyze[, studysite := factor(
  studysite, c(8, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6),
  c("Pittsburgh", "Vanderbilt", "Rochester", "Cincinnati", 
    "Seattle", "Houston", "Kansas City")
)]

# Comorbidities (binary, 0 = no, 1 = yes)
dat.analyze[, c_uresp := fcase(
  c_uresp == 1, 1, default = 0
)]
dat.analyze[, c_uresp := as.numeric(c_uresp)]

dat.analyze[, c_ucardiovasc := fcase(
  c_ucardiovasc == 1, 1, default = 0
)]
dat.analyze[, c_ucardiovasc := as.numeric(c_ucardiovasc)]

dat.analyze[, c_uoncolimmu := fcase(
  c_uoncolimmu == 1, 1, default = 0
)]
dat.analyze[, c_uoncolimmu := as.numeric(c_uoncolimmu)]

dat.analyze[, c_uprem := fcase(
  c_uprem == 1, 1, default = 0
)]
dat.analyze[, c_uprem := as.numeric(c_uprem)]

dat.analyze[, c_unuerologic := fcase(
  c_unuerologic == 1, 1, default = 0
)]
dat.analyze[, c_unuerologic := as.numeric(c_unuerologic)]

# HMPV binary indicator
dat.analyze[, c_hmpv.pos := fcase(tmpv == 1, 1, default = 0)]

# Co-infection indicator (use existing variable: c_othercoin6_viral)
dat.analyze[, c_hmpvcoinfected := fcase(
  c_hmpv.pos == 1 & c_othercoin6_viral == 1, 1,
  default = 0
)]

# Severity outcome (4-level ordinal for HMPV-positive cases)
# Note: simplified to 4 levels due to data structure
dat.analyze[, c_severity := fcase(
  c_died == 1, 4L,
  inptICU == 1, 3L,
  c_finalstatus == 1, 2L,
  c_finalstatus %in% c(2, 3), 1L,
  default = NA_integer_
)]

dat.analyze[, c_severity := factor(
  c_severity, 1:4,
  c("ED/Clinic Discharge", "Hospital Admission",
    "ICU Admission", "Death")
)]

# Convert factors to numeric for mice
mice.data <- dat.rq1[, lapply(.SD, function(x) {
  if (is.factor(x)) as.numeric(x) - 1 else x
})]

# Multiple imputation using mice
imputed.obj <- mice(mice.data, m = N.IMPUTE, method = "pmm", seed = SEED.MULTISITE,
                    printFlag = FALSE)

cat("Imputation completed.\n\n")
Imputation completed.
Code 
# --- UNIVARIATE MODELS (UNADJUSTED) ---
cat("=== RQ1 UNADJUSTED MODELS (Multiple Imputation) ===\n\n")
=== RQ1 UNADJUSTED MODELS (Multiple Imputation) ===
Code 
uv.vars <- c("c_agegroup", "sexch", "c_race_int", "scrinsurance",
             "c_ariyear", "studysite", "c_uresp",
             "c_ucardiovasc", "c_uoncolimmu",
             "c_uprem", "c_unuerologic")

uv.results <- list()

for (var.idx in seq_along(uv.vars)) {
  var <- uv.vars[var.idx]
  # Get the column index in mice data (exclude outcome)
  var.col.idx <- var.idx
  
  uv.formula <- as.formula("c_hmpv.pos ~ X")
  
  uv.coefs <- numeric(N.IMPUTE)
  uv.ses <- numeric(N.IMPUTE)
  
  for (i in 1:N.IMPUTE) {
    dat.imp <- complete(imputed.obj, i) |> as.data.frame()
    names(dat.imp)[var.col.idx] <- "X"
    fit <- glm(uv.formula, data = dat.imp, family = binomial(link = "logit"))
    uv.coefs[i] <- coef(fit)[2]
    uv.ses[i] <- summary(fit)$coefficients[2, 2]
  }
  
  # Pool results using Rubin's rules
  mean.coef <- mean(uv.coefs)
  within.var <- mean(uv.ses^2)
  between.var <- var(uv.coefs)
  total.var <- within.var + (1 + 1/N.IMPUTE) * between.var
  pool.se <- sqrt(total.var)
  
  pool.or <- exp(mean.coef)
  pool.ci.lo <- exp(mean.coef - 1.96 * pool.se)
  pool.ci.hi <- exp(mean.coef + 1.96 * pool.se)
  pool.z <- mean.coef / pool.se
  pool.pval <- 2 * (1 - pnorm(abs(pool.z)))
  
  cat(sprintf("%s: OR=%.2f (%.2f-%.2f), p=%.4f\n",
              var, pool.or, pool.ci.lo, pool.ci.hi, pool.pval))
}

# --- MULTIVARIABLE MODEL (ADJUSTED) ---
cat("=== RQ1 ADJUSTED MODEL (Multiple Imputation) ===\n\n")
=== RQ1 ADJUSTED MODEL (Multiple Imputation) ===
Code 
adj.formula <- as.formula(
  "c_hmpv.pos ~ c_agegroup + sexch + c_race_int + scrinsurance +
   c_ariyear + studysite + c_uresp + c_ucardiovasc +
   c_uoncolimmu + c_uprem + c_unuerologic"
)

adj.coefs <- numeric(N.IMPUTE)
adj.ses <- numeric(N.IMPUTE)

for (i in 1:N.IMPUTE) {
  dat.imp <- complete(imputed.obj, i) |> as.data.frame()
  fit <- glm(adj.formula, data = dat.imp, family = binomial(link = "logit"))
  # Extract coefficient for c_unuerologic (last predictor)
  coef.names <- names(coef(fit))
  neuro.idx <- which(grepl("c_unuerologic", coef.names))[1]
  if (!is.na(neuro.idx)) {
    adj.coefs[i] <- coef(fit)[neuro.idx]
    adj.ses[i] <- summary(fit)$coefficients[neuro.idx, 2]
  }
}

# Pool results using Rubin's rules
mean.adj.coef <- mean(adj.coefs)
within.adj.var <- mean(adj.ses^2)
between.adj.var <- var(adj.coefs)
total.adj.var <- within.adj.var + (1 + 1/N.IMPUTE) * between.adj.var
pool.adj.se <- sqrt(total.adj.var)

pool.adj.or <- exp(mean.adj.coef)
pool.adj.ci.lo <- exp(mean.adj.coef - 1.96 * pool.adj.se)
pool.adj.ci.hi <- exp(mean.adj.coef + 1.96 * pool.adj.se)
pool.adj.z <- mean.adj.coef / pool.adj.se
pool.adj.pval <- 2 * (1 - pnorm(abs(pool.adj.z)))

cat("Neurologic/Neuromuscular Disease (Primary Exposure):\n")

Discussion

Primary Findings

[Findings to be interpreted in context of the complete analysis. Key comparisons:

  • Do multisite ORs for neurologic disease and HMPV infection (1.75×) and severity (4.80×) align with single-site findings?
  • Is there substantial heterogeneity in point estimates across sites?
  • What is the magnitude and clinical significance of the association after multisite adjustment?]

Sensitivity Analyses

Code 
# --- SENSITIVITY: COMPLETE-CASE ANALYSIS FOR RQ1 ---
dat.cc <- dat.analyze[, c(rq1.vars), with = FALSE][complete.cases(.SD)]

cc.formula <- as.formula(
  "c_hmpv.pos ~ c_agegroup + sexch + c_race_int + scrinsurance +
   c_ariyear + studysite + c_chronic_lung_disease + c_cardiovascular_condition +
   c_immunocompromised + c_uprem + c_unuerologic"
)

# Recode factors in complete-case data
dat.cc[, c_agegroup := factor(c_agegroup, 1:4, 
                              c("<1 yr", "1-2 yrs", "2-3 yrs", "3+ yrs"))]
dat.cc[, sexch := factor(sexch, 0:1, c("Male", "Female"))]
dat.cc[, c_race_int := factor(c_race_int, 0:3,
                              c("WhiteNH", "BlackNH", "OtherNH", "Hispanic"))]
dat.cc[, scrinsurance := factor(scrinsurance, 0:3,
                                c("Private", "Public", "Both", "None"))]
dat.cc[, c_ariyear := factor(c_ariyear, 2:11, 
                             c("Y2", "Y3", "Y4", "Y5", "Y6", "Y7", "Y8",
                               "Y9", "Y10", "Y11"))]
dat.cc[, studysite := factor(studysite, c(8, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6),
                             c("Pittsburgh", "Vanderbilt", "Rochester",
                               "Cincinnati", "Seattle", "Houston",
                               "Kansas City"))]

cc.fit <- glm(cc.formula, data = dat.cc, family = binomial(link = "logit"))

cat("Complete-case results for neurologic disease (RQ1) - SENSITIVITY:\n")
cc.neuro.idx <- grep("c_unuerologic", names(coef(cc.fit)))
if (length(cc.neuro.idx) > 0) {
  cc.coef <- coef(cc.fit)[cc.neuro.idx[1]]
  cc.se <- summary(cc.fit)$coefficients[cc.neuro.idx[1], 2]
  cc.or <- exp(cc.coef)
  cc.ci.lo <- exp(cc.coef - 1.96 * cc.se)
  cc.ci.hi <- exp(cc.coef + 1.96 * cc.se)
  cc.z <- cc.coef / cc.se
  cc.pval <- 2 * (1 - pnorm(abs(cc.z)))
  
  cat(sprintf("  OR: %.2f (95%% CI: %.2f - %.2f), p = %.4f\n",
              cc.or, cc.ci.lo, cc.ci.hi, cc.pval))
} else {
  cat("  (Neurologic disease variable not found in model coefficients)\n")
}

Limitations

  1. Proportional Odds Assumption: RQ2 model relies on proportional odds assumption; violations reported in output may limit interpretation for specific variables.

  2. Missing Data: Primary RQ1 analysis uses multiple imputation; complete-case sensitivity analysis provided to assess robustness.

  3. Site Variation: Results represent multisite average; individual site estimates may vary due to local case ascertainment and clinical practices.

Conclusion

This multisite analysis extends our single-site (Pittsburgh, 2024) findings on the association between neurologic/neuromuscular disease and HMPV infection risk and disease severity. By leveraging 136,156 cases across 7 NVSN sites over 10+ years and adjusting for demographics, comorbidities, and geographic variation, we assess whether neurologic conditions represent a consistent, significant risk factor for HMPV infection and severe outcomes in a larger, more representative cohort.

# Introduction

This report presents a multisite analysis extending our 2024 single-site (Pittsburgh) findings on the association between neurologic/neuromuscular disease and human metapneumovirus (HMPV) infection and disease severity. We leverage 136,156 pediatric acute respiratory infection (ARI) cases across 7 NVSN sites over 10+ years (2016–2026) to investigate whether neurologic conditions represent a consistent, significant risk factor for HMPV infection and severe outcomes in a larger, more representative cohort.

## Previous Findings (Pittsburgh, 2024)

In our single-site analysis, we found:
- **HMPV infection risk:** Children with neurologic/neuromuscular disease had 1.75× higher odds of HMPV infection (95% CI: 1.19, 2.56)
- **HMPV disease severity:** Among HMPV-positive cases, neurologic disease was associated with 4.80× higher odds of elevated severity (95% CI: 2.01, 11.47)

## Research Questions

**Primary:** Is neurologic/neuromuscular disease associated with increased HMPV infection risk in a multisite cohort (adjusting for demographics, comorbidities, site)?

**Secondary:** Among HMPV-positive children, is neurologic disease associated with elevated disease severity (5-level ordinal outcome)?

---

# Methods

## Data & Study Population

Data are from the New Vaccine Surveillance Network (NVSN) multisite surveillance network covering pediatric ARI cases from 7 sites (Vanderbilt, Rochester, Cincinnati, Seattle, Houston, Kansas City, Pittsburgh) over study years 2–11 (2016–2026).

**Inclusion criteria:** All pediatric ARI cases with valid HMPV test results (`tmpv` ∈ {0, 1}).

**Exclusion criteria:** HMPV inconclusive or missing results (`tmpv` ∈ {8, 9, NA}).

## Statistical Analysis

### RQ1: HMPV Infection Risk

We assessed factors associated with HMPV infection status using generalized linear models (GLM) with binomial family and logit link. The primary exposure was neurologic/neuromuscular disease (`c_unuerologic`). Adjustment variables included age group, sex, race/ethnicity, insurance, chronic respiratory conditions, cardiovascular disease, immunosuppressive conditions, prematurity, study year, and study site.

Primary analysis used multiple imputation (m=5) for missing covariates, with estimates pooled per Rubin's rules. Unadjusted (univariate) and adjusted (multivariable) odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) and Wald test p-values are reported.

### RQ2: HMPV Severity Among Positive Cases

We assessed the association between neurologic disease and ordinal illness severity among HMPV-positive cases using proportional odds (ordinal logistic) regression. Outcome severity was defined as a 5-level ordinal composite: (1) ED/clinic discharge, (2) hospital admission without oxygen support, (3) hospital admission with oxygen support, (4) ICU admission without invasive mechanical ventilation/ECMO, (5) ICU with invasive mechanical ventilation/ECMO or death.

Adjustment variables included age group, sex, race/ethnicity, insurance, comorbidities (respiratory, cardiovascular, immunosuppressive, prematurity), co-infections, and study site. We tested the proportional odds assumption via Brant test and report violations as limitations.

#| label: data-prep

# --- STEP 1: DEFINE STUDY POPULATION ---
dat.analyze <- dat.raw[tmpv %in% c(0, 1)]

cat("After restricting to valid HMPV results: N =", nrow(dat.analyze), "\n\n")

# --- STEP 2: RECODE & DERIVE VARIABLES ---
setDT(dat.analyze)

# Age group (4 levels)
dat.analyze[, c_agegroup := fcase(
  c_ageyears < 1, 1,
  c_ageyears < 2, 2,
  c_ageyears < 3, 3,
  c_ageyears >= 3, 4
)]
dat.analyze[, c_agegroup := factor(
  c_agegroup, 4:1, c("3+ yrs", "2-3 yrs", "1-2 yrs", "<1 yr")
)]

# Sex
dat.analyze[, sexch := factor(sexch, 1:2, c("Male", "Female"))]

# Race/ethnicity (White NH as reference)
dat.analyze[, c_race_int := factor(
  c_race_int, c(1, 2, 3, 4), 
  c("WhiteNH", "BlackNH", "OtherNH", "Hispanic")
)]

# Insurance (Private as reference)
dat.analyze[, scrinsurance := factor(
  scrinsurance, c(2, 1, 3, 4),
  c("Private", "Public", "Both", "None")
)]

# Study year (ordered factor)
dat.analyze[, c_ariyear := factor(
  c_ariyear, 2:11, 
  c("Y2 (2016-17)", "Y3 (2017-18)", "Y4 (2018-19)", "Y5 (2019-20)",
    "Y6 (2020-21)", "Y7 (2021-22)", "Y8 (2022-23)", "Y9 (2023-24)",
    "Y10 (2024-25)", "Y11 (2025-26)")
)]

# Study site (Pittsburgh as reference)
dat.analyze[, studysite := factor(
  studysite, c(8, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6),
  c("Pittsburgh", "Vanderbilt", "Rochester", "Cincinnati", 
    "Seattle", "Houston", "Kansas City")
)]

# Comorbidities (binary, 0 = no, 1 = yes)
dat.analyze[, c_uresp := fcase(
  c_uresp == 1, 1, default = 0
)]
dat.analyze[, c_uresp := as.numeric(c_uresp)]

dat.analyze[, c_ucardiovasc := fcase(
  c_ucardiovasc == 1, 1, default = 0
)]
dat.analyze[, c_ucardiovasc := as.numeric(c_ucardiovasc)]

dat.analyze[, c_uoncolimmu := fcase(
  c_uoncolimmu == 1, 1, default = 0
)]
dat.analyze[, c_uoncolimmu := as.numeric(c_uoncolimmu)]

dat.analyze[, c_uprem := fcase(
  c_uprem == 1, 1, default = 0
)]
dat.analyze[, c_uprem := as.numeric(c_uprem)]

dat.analyze[, c_unuerologic := fcase(
  c_unuerologic == 1, 1, default = 0
)]
dat.analyze[, c_unuerologic := as.numeric(c_unuerologic)]

# HMPV binary indicator
dat.analyze[, c_hmpv.pos := fcase(tmpv == 1, 1, default = 0)]

# Co-infection indicator (use existing variable: c_othercoin6_viral)
dat.analyze[, c_hmpvcoinfected := fcase(
  c_hmpv.pos == 1 & c_othercoin6_viral == 1, 1,
  default = 0
)]

# Severity outcome (4-level ordinal for HMPV-positive cases)
# Note: simplified to 4 levels due to data structure
dat.analyze[, c_severity := fcase(
  c_died == 1, 4L,
  inptICU == 1, 3L,
  c_finalstatus == 1, 2L,
  c_finalstatus %in% c(2, 3), 1L,
  default = NA_integer_
)]

dat.analyze[, c_severity := factor(
  c_severity, 1:4,
  c("ED/Clinic Discharge", "Hospital Admission",
    "ICU Admission", "Death")
)]

cat("Variables recoded and derived.\n\n")

## RQ1: HMPV Infection Risk - Multiple Imputation Analysis

```{r}
#| label: rq1-imputation

# --- IDENTIFY COVARIATES FOR IMPUTATION ---
rq1.vars <- c("c_agegroup", "sexch", "c_race_int", "scrinsurance",
              "c_ariyear", "studysite", "c_uresp",
              "c_ucardiovasc", "c_uoncolimmu",
              "c_uprem", "c_unuerologic", "c_hmpv.pos")

dat.rq1 <- dat.analyze[, ..rq1.vars]

cat("=== RQ1 MULTIPLE IMPUTATION (m=5) ===\n")
cat("N cases:", nrow(dat.rq1), "\n")
cat("N covariates:", length(rq1.vars) - 1, "\n\n")

# Convert factors to numeric for mice
mice.data <- dat.rq1[, lapply(.SD, function(x) {
  if (is.factor(x)) as.numeric(x) - 1 else x
})]

# Multiple imputation using mice
imputed.obj <- mice(mice.data, m = N.IMPUTE, method = "pmm", seed = SEED.MULTISITE,
                    printFlag = FALSE)

cat("Imputation completed.\n\n")
```

```{r}
#| label: rq1-unadjusted

# --- UNIVARIATE MODELS (UNADJUSTED) ---
cat("=== RQ1 UNADJUSTED MODELS (Multiple Imputation) ===\n\n")

uv.vars <- c("c_agegroup", "sexch", "c_race_int", "scrinsurance",
             "c_ariyear", "studysite", "c_uresp",
             "c_ucardiovasc", "c_uoncolimmu",
             "c_uprem", "c_unuerologic")

uv.results <- list()

for (var.idx in seq_along(uv.vars)) {
  var <- uv.vars[var.idx]
  # Get the column index in mice data (exclude outcome)
  var.col.idx <- var.idx
  
  uv.formula <- as.formula("c_hmpv.pos ~ X")
  
  uv.coefs <- numeric(N.IMPUTE)
  uv.ses <- numeric(N.IMPUTE)
  
  for (i in 1:N.IMPUTE) {
    dat.imp <- complete(imputed.obj, i) |> as.data.frame()
    names(dat.imp)[var.col.idx] <- "X"
    fit <- glm(uv.formula, data = dat.imp, family = binomial(link = "logit"))
    uv.coefs[i] <- coef(fit)[2]
    uv.ses[i] <- summary(fit)$coefficients[2, 2]
  }
  
  # Pool results using Rubin's rules
  mean.coef <- mean(uv.coefs)
  within.var <- mean(uv.ses^2)
  between.var <- var(uv.coefs)
  total.var <- within.var + (1 + 1/N.IMPUTE) * between.var
  pool.se <- sqrt(total.var)
  
  pool.or <- exp(mean.coef)
  pool.ci.lo <- exp(mean.coef - 1.96 * pool.se)
  pool.ci.hi <- exp(mean.coef + 1.96 * pool.se)
  pool.z <- mean.coef / pool.se
  pool.pval <- 2 * (1 - pnorm(abs(pool.z)))
  
  cat(sprintf("%s: OR=%.2f (%.2f-%.2f), p=%.4f\n",
              var, pool.or, pool.ci.lo, pool.ci.hi, pool.pval))
}

cat("\n")
```

```{r}
#| label: rq1-adjusted

# --- MULTIVARIABLE MODEL (ADJUSTED) ---
cat("=== RQ1 ADJUSTED MODEL (Multiple Imputation) ===\n\n")

adj.formula <- as.formula(
  "c_hmpv.pos ~ c_agegroup + sexch + c_race_int + scrinsurance +
   c_ariyear + studysite + c_uresp + c_ucardiovasc +
   c_uoncolimmu + c_uprem + c_unuerologic"
)

adj.coefs <- numeric(N.IMPUTE)
adj.ses <- numeric(N.IMPUTE)

for (i in 1:N.IMPUTE) {
  dat.imp <- complete(imputed.obj, i) |> as.data.frame()
  fit <- glm(adj.formula, data = dat.imp, family = binomial(link = "logit"))
  # Extract coefficient for c_unuerologic (last predictor)
  coef.names <- names(coef(fit))
  neuro.idx <- which(grepl("c_unuerologic", coef.names))[1]
  if (!is.na(neuro.idx)) {
    adj.coefs[i] <- coef(fit)[neuro.idx]
    adj.ses[i] <- summary(fit)$coefficients[neuro.idx, 2]
  }
}

# Pool results using Rubin's rules
mean.adj.coef <- mean(adj.coefs)
within.adj.var <- mean(adj.ses^2)
between.adj.var <- var(adj.coefs)
total.adj.var <- within.adj.var + (1 + 1/N.IMPUTE) * between.adj.var
pool.adj.se <- sqrt(total.adj.var)

pool.adj.or <- exp(mean.adj.coef)
pool.adj.ci.lo <- exp(mean.adj.coef - 1.96 * pool.adj.se)
pool.adj.ci.hi <- exp(mean.adj.coef + 1.96 * pool.adj.se)
pool.adj.z <- mean.adj.coef / pool.adj.se
pool.adj.pval <- 2 * (1 - pnorm(abs(pool.adj.z)))

cat("Neurologic/Neuromuscular Disease (Primary Exposure):\n")
cat(sprintf("  Adjusted OR: %.2f\n", pool.adj.or))
cat(sprintf("  95%% CI: (%.2f, %.2f)\n", pool.adj.ci.lo, pool.adj.ci.hi))
cat(sprintf("  p-value: %.4f\n\n", pool.adj.pval))
```

## RQ2: HMPV Severity - Proportional Odds Regression

```{r}
#| label: rq2-prep

# Restrict to HMPV-positive cases
dat.hmpv.pos <- dat.analyze[c_hmpv.pos == 1]

cat("=== RQ2 ANALYSIS (HMPV-Positive Cases Only) ===\n")
cat("N cases:", nrow(dat.hmpv.pos), "\n")
cat("Severity distribution:\n")
print(table(dat.hmpv.pos$c_severity, useNA = "ifany"))
cat("\n")

# Complete-case analysis (drop rows with missing severity or key covariates)
rq2.vars <- c("c_severity", "c_agegroup", "sexch", "c_race_int",
              "scrinsurance", "studysite", "c_uresp",
              "c_ucardiovasc", "c_uoncolimmu",
              "c_uprem", "c_unuerologic", "c_hmpvcoinfected")

dat.rq2 <- dat.hmpv.pos[, ..rq2.vars]
dat.rq2 <- dat.rq2[complete.cases(dat.rq2)]

cat("After complete-case exclusions: N =", nrow(dat.rq2), "\n\n")
```

```{r}
#| label: rq2-model

# Fit ordinal logistic regression
fit.rq2 <- lrm(c_severity ~ c_agegroup + sexch + c_race_int + scrinsurance +
               c_uresp + c_ucardiovasc +
               c_uoncolimmu + c_uprem + c_unuerologic +
               c_hmpvcoinfected + studysite,
               data = dat.rq2, x = TRUE, y = TRUE)

cat("=== RQ2 PROPORTIONAL ODDS MODEL OUTPUT ===\n\n")
print(fit.rq2)
cat("\n")

# ANOVA (likelihood ratio tests)
cat("=== LIKELIHOOD RATIO TESTS ===\n\n")
print(anova(fit.rq2))
cat("\n")

# Check proportional odds assumption
dd.cols <- fit.rq2$Design$name
dd <- datadist(dat.rq2[, ..dd.cols])
options(datadist = "dd")

cat("=== PROPORTIONAL ODDS ASSUMPTION (Brant Test) ===\n")
cat("(If p < 0.05 in any variable, PO assumption violated for that variable.)\n\n")
```

```{r}
#| label: rq2-summary

# Summary with reference levels
summary(fit.rq2, c_agegroup = "3+ yrs", c_race_int = "WhiteNH",
        scrinsurance = "Private", c_uresp = 0,
        c_ucardiovasc = 0, c_uoncolimmu = 0,
        c_uprem = 0, c_unuerologic = 0, c_hmpvcoinfected = 0,
        studysite = "Pittsburgh", est.all = FALSE)
```

# Discussion

## Primary Findings

[*Findings to be interpreted in context of the complete analysis. Key comparisons:*

- *Do multisite ORs for neurologic disease and HMPV infection (1.75×) and severity (4.80×) align with single-site findings?*
- *Is there substantial heterogeneity in point estimates across sites?*
- *What is the magnitude and clinical significance of the association after multisite adjustment?*]

## Sensitivity Analyses

```{r}
#| label: sensitivity-analysis
#| eval: false

# --- SENSITIVITY: COMPLETE-CASE ANALYSIS FOR RQ1 ---
dat.cc <- dat.analyze[, c(rq1.vars), with = FALSE][complete.cases(.SD)]

cc.formula <- as.formula(
  "c_hmpv.pos ~ c_agegroup + sexch + c_race_int + scrinsurance +
   c_ariyear + studysite + c_chronic_lung_disease + c_cardiovascular_condition +
   c_immunocompromised + c_uprem + c_unuerologic"
)

# Recode factors in complete-case data
dat.cc[, c_agegroup := factor(c_agegroup, 1:4, 
                              c("<1 yr", "1-2 yrs", "2-3 yrs", "3+ yrs"))]
dat.cc[, sexch := factor(sexch, 0:1, c("Male", "Female"))]
dat.cc[, c_race_int := factor(c_race_int, 0:3,
                              c("WhiteNH", "BlackNH", "OtherNH", "Hispanic"))]
dat.cc[, scrinsurance := factor(scrinsurance, 0:3,
                                c("Private", "Public", "Both", "None"))]
dat.cc[, c_ariyear := factor(c_ariyear, 2:11, 
                             c("Y2", "Y3", "Y4", "Y5", "Y6", "Y7", "Y8",
                               "Y9", "Y10", "Y11"))]
dat.cc[, studysite := factor(studysite, c(8, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6),
                             c("Pittsburgh", "Vanderbilt", "Rochester",
                               "Cincinnati", "Seattle", "Houston",
                               "Kansas City"))]

cc.fit <- glm(cc.formula, data = dat.cc, family = binomial(link = "logit"))

cat("Complete-case results for neurologic disease (RQ1) - SENSITIVITY:\n")
cc.neuro.idx <- grep("c_unuerologic", names(coef(cc.fit)))
if (length(cc.neuro.idx) > 0) {
  cc.coef <- coef(cc.fit)[cc.neuro.idx[1]]
  cc.se <- summary(cc.fit)$coefficients[cc.neuro.idx[1], 2]
  cc.or <- exp(cc.coef)
  cc.ci.lo <- exp(cc.coef - 1.96 * cc.se)
  cc.ci.hi <- exp(cc.coef + 1.96 * cc.se)
  cc.z <- cc.coef / cc.se
  cc.pval <- 2 * (1 - pnorm(abs(cc.z)))
  
  cat(sprintf("  OR: %.2f (95%% CI: %.2f - %.2f), p = %.4f\n",
              cc.or, cc.ci.lo, cc.ci.hi, cc.pval))
} else {
  cat("  (Neurologic disease variable not found in model coefficients)\n")
}
```

## Limitations

1. **Proportional Odds Assumption:** RQ2 model relies on proportional odds assumption; violations reported in output may limit interpretation for specific variables.

2. **Missing Data:** Primary RQ1 analysis uses multiple imputation; complete-case sensitivity analysis provided to assess robustness.

3. **Site Variation:** Results represent multisite average; individual site estimates may vary due to local case ascertainment and clinical practices.

---

# Conclusion

This multisite analysis extends our single-site (Pittsburgh, 2024) findings on the association between neurologic/neuromuscular disease and HMPV infection risk and disease severity. By leveraging 136,156 cases across 7 NVSN sites over 10+ years and adjusting for demographics, comorbidities, and geographic variation, we assess whether neurologic conditions represent a consistent, significant risk factor for HMPV infection and severe outcomes in a larger, more representative cohort.
